# Summary of Information on University College London (UCL)
University College London (UCL) was founded in 1826 as London University and later became University College, London in 1836. Initially an alternative to the Anglican universities Oxford and Cambridge, UCL became a founding college of the University of London. Over its history, UCL expanded through mergers, regained legal independence in 1976, and was granted the power to award its own degrees in 2005. It adopted the branding "UCL" and opened a secondary campus, UCL East, in Stratford, London, in 2022. UCL was granted university status in 2023, while remaining part of the University of London. It is located primarily in Bloomsbury, Central London, with multiple specialized institutes and associated teaching hospitals across London.
UCL is a major research university and a founding member of the Russell Group and the League of European Research Universities, operating numerous research centers such as the London Centre for Nanotechnology and the Centre for the Study of the Legacies of British Slave-ownership. In 2023/24, research income totaled £538.8 million, with a significant proportion rated as world-leading in the 2021 Research Excellence Framework. UCL has an extensive library system with over 2 million books across 18 libraries, including significant special collections with rare editions from Isaac Newton and Charles Darwin. The university runs several museums, including the Petrie Museum of Egyptian Archaeology and the Grant Museum of Zoology. UCL Press, launched in 2015, is the first fully open access university press in the UK.
Admission to UCL is highly selective, with average entry requirements equivalent to AAAB at A-level and an undergraduate offer rate of 36.1% in 2021. International students have formed the majority of offers since 2017. UCL operates widening access schemes, such as Access UCL and foundation year programs, to increase opportunities for disadvantaged applicants. The student body is diverse, with about 24% British white students, 24% British ethnic minorities, 7% EU international students, and 46% non-EU international students; females constitute 58%. UCL owns 26 halls of residence housing approximately 7,000 students and guarantees accommodation to eligible first-year students.
Governance is led by a council and academic board established by royal charter, with the President and Provost as the chief executive officer. The university comprises eleven faculties covering disciplines from arts and humanities to medical sciences, with over 12,000 staff and a diverse student population exceeding 45,000. UCL is recognized nationally and globally for teaching quality, research power, and sustainability, being named University of the Year in the 2024 Times/Sunday Times Good University Guide and ranking within the top 10 globally by multiple rankings.
